title: Inquest into three police shootings set for Oct. 15
subtitle: Coming prior to Sammy Yatim's streetcar shooting, all three deaths to be examined involved people thought to be mentally ill.
article: An inquest into the police shooting deaths of three GTA residents who may have been in a mental-health crisis while wielding knives and scissors has finally been set for the fall.

The announcement from the Chief Coroner's office comes less than two weeks after yet another fatal police shooting in Toronto raised public outrage, and on the same day the province's ombudsman launched an investigation into police training.

More than 50 witnesses are expected at the inquest, which will start Oct. 15 and last eight weeks. The inquest will cover the deaths of Reyal Jardine-Douglas , 25; Sylvia Klibingaitis , 52; and Michael Eligon , 29 - all shot by Toronto police officers.

Klibingaitis was killed the morning of Oct. 7, 2011, after she called police to her North York home saying she had a knife and was going to commit a crime, according to the Special Investigations Unit. Klibingaitis, whose family said she experienced psychosis and suffered from bipolar disorder, was shot once in the chest by a Toronto police officer, of three rounds fired.

Klibingaitis' sister, Anita Wasowicz, said she still struggles to understand why her death occurred despite the recommendations made by previous inquests into similar shootings - like that of mentally ill Edmond Yu , who was gunned down on a Spadina bus in 1997. Though police were cleared in the shooting, Yu's death and subsequent inquest prompted specialized training for police in dealing with mental illness.

"As much as I have hope, the point is I had hope 15 to 16 years ago," said Wasowicz, now a mental health advocate. "I don't understand, still, why we're seeing these problems continue even after Sylvia was killed."

Last week, Wasowicz walked down Dundas St. holding her sister's picture during a vigil demanding justice for 18-year-old Sammy Yatim . Yatim was shot, then Tasered, on an empty streetcar on July 27 after police were called to the scene and found Yatim holding a knife. Const. James Forcillo is the subject of an ongoing SIU investigation after nine shots were fired, as heard in a bystander video.
Wasowicz said she is apprehensive about the upcoming inquest and doesn't know what to expect in terms of an outcome.
"I'm not sure what the actual steps will be in the future, because again, it should have been done by now," she said.

The deaths of all three included in the upcoming inquest drew controversy over police tactics and questions over whether officers were equipped to de-escalate situations involving mentally ill people.

Pickering man Jardine-Douglas died on Aug. 29, 2010, after his family called the police to admit their mentally ill son to hospital. Police found Jardine-Douglas on a Victoria Park bus, where the SIU later said he had advanced on a Toronto police officer with a knife. The officer fired four times, hitting Jardine-Douglas twice, the SIU said.

Michael Eligon was killed on Feb. 3, 2012, after escaping Toronto East General Hospital, where he had been admitted under the Mental Health Act. Eligon, still wearing a hospital gown and holding two pairs of scissors, was shot once while surrounded by 12 officers, the SIU said. Three rounds were fired.
In all three cases, SIU director Ian Scott ruled the officers had been justified in using lethal force.

A coroner's inquest is mandatory where two or more deaths occur from a " common cause ," the coroner's office said in the release. A jury cannot make findings of guilt, only recommendations "aimed at preventing similar deaths."

In past inquests, some of those recommendations have included giving all frontline officers access to Tasers - an idea that has remained controversial with the public after numerous instances of death following Tasering.

Toronto officers receive two days of mandatory use-of-force training annually that includes how to handle people with mental illness and how to de-escalate volatile situations using communication skills.
The inquest will be held at the new Forensic Services and Coroner's Complex in North York.
